ratings.reason: A clear accept/cancel disposition for the current suggestion, with unusually precise feedback and keyboard behavior. It is not a perfect structural match: controls are not shown as co-located with every item, continuing to type provides another rejection path, and the quote describes one active preview rather than a collection of independently actionable items. The interaction is highly reusable but conventional.

The accept/regenerate/edit vocabulary is a clean disposition set in the later workflow steps. However, the action set changes across steps—regenerate alone first, then three actions—so it is not constant across the full session as required by the signature. Useful and transferable, but a standard co-creation control scheme.

Incorporate, ignore, or request another recommendation is a clear, closed vocabulary for disposing of LLM text. The quote does not explicitly establish co-location or multiple independently actionable items, but otherwise closely fits the pattern. Its application to sensitive journaling matters, while the interaction itself is settled and unsurprising.

Approve, edit, or replace is a recognizable fixed disposition set, and human moderation makes these choices consequential. The evidence does not say whether controls are attached uniformly to each suggestion or whether other disposition paths exist. Applying the familiar pattern to real-time Wizard-of-Oz moderation is more interesting than the controls themselves.

Adopt, edit, or dismiss is the canonical pattern vocabulary, but the abstract-level quote does not establish per-suggestion attachment, co-location, or session-wide constancy. The randomized-trial title signals strong overall outcomes, yet the supplied evidence cannot attribute those outcomes specifically to these controls. As a design move, it is highly conventional.

The quote explicitly identifies an accept/reject interface applied to several concrete transformations, making this a strong instance. It does not quite confirm that every transformation has its own co-located controls and independent state. The reversible application of sustainability fixes is consequential and broadly transferable, though binary acceptance itself is familiar.

Accept, reject, or refine is an enumerable vocabulary, but the controls occur in settings and may operate on tags as configuration rather than on individually rendered generated items. The quote does not resolve whether tags are handled one at a time. Autonomy is important in emotional journaling, but the interaction is ordinary.

The fragment only names categories in a temporal distribution. It does not establish that Delegate, Expansion, and Dismissal are interface controls, that they act on system-produced items, or that they form a per-item closed disposition set. Impact and mechanism therefore cannot be judged from the supplied evidence.
ratings.disqualify_reason: The evidence quote does not support the pattern assignment: it reports category labels in a figure without demonstrating per-item accept/reject controls or even an actionable interface mechanism.

ratings.reason: A panel listing flagged issues alongside acknowledge/dismiss actions is close to the required repeated per-item control group. The quote does not explicitly say whether each issue is independently handled or whether the action set is exhaustive, but the intended mechanism is readily reconstructable. This is useful auditing UI, though a familiar issue-triage pattern.

Accept and modify are relevant dispositions, but the quote is truncated before the action set is completed and says nothing about per-item attachment, co-location, or exclusivity. The title suggests an interesting creator–curator framing, but the supplied fragment is too incomplete to connect that contribution confidently to this pattern.

Each candidate is explicitly editable and assigned to one of three fixed dispositions: positive example, negative example, or excluded. This is an unusually clean and reconstructable instance of uniform per-item controls. More importantly, disposition choices become demonstrations that shape later model behavior, moving the design beyond routine acceptance while remaining broadly portable.

The binary swipe vocabulary is exceptionally clear, but it expresses a pairwise preference between current and previous images rather than an independent disposition attached to each item. One action necessarily concerns two items and likely steers subsequent exploration, so this is principally preference elicitation rather than accept/reject control. The interaction is interesting, but not representative of this pattern.

Kudos, critique, and rewrite form a small fixed vocabulary, but the quote calls them features and does not show that identical controls accompany each generated principle or suggestion. Converting distinct feedback dispositions into principles could be consequential and non-obvious, but that connection cannot be established from the figure caption alone.

“For each recommendation” supports the individual-item unit, but “various actions” neither enumerates a closed vocabulary nor explains what any action does. The evidence therefore supplies only the outer shape of the pattern. No pattern-specific impact or novelty can be judged from what is present.

Accept, trim, merge, or demote is a concrete, enumerable action vocabulary for generated markers. It departs from the signature because merge inherently affects multiple markers, and the quote does not establish co-located controls or exhaustiveness. The richer dispositions plausibly improve video-editing control, but some operations are domain-specific.

This is the clearest literal match: every suggestion can be previewed, applied, undone, or regenerated individually, and the evidence explicitly emphasizes independent handling. The workflow materially supports incremental construction of a complex VR scene and is reconstructable from the quote. The application is notable, although the disposition vocabulary itself is established rather than radical.

Accept and Reject are explicit controls with concrete, distinct system consequences for the current patch. This is a strong canonical instance, though the quote describes one active patch rather than showing repeated co-located groups across multiple items, and rejection can branch into clarification. Direct patch application makes the choice consequential, but the interaction is standard.

Regenerate and Pin appear to dispose of a character highlight, while View is navigation rather than disposition. The truncated caption does not establish a complete closed set, identical controls across highlights, or independent item handling. The mechanism may support accessible game modding, but its fit and pattern-specific contribution are underdetermined by the supplied evidence.
